subject.title: [Feature]: Host-owned restrictive policy for embedded ACP sessions

question: Which component owns the non-bypassable pre-execution enforcement decision for embedded ACP sessions: ACPX, the ACP runtime/adapter, or a jointly specified split contract?
rationale: The requested guarantee depends on controls below remote-chat configuration and cannot be safely inferred from the current coarse permission-mode surface or a provider-specific option channel.

options.title: Define a shared runtime contract
options.body: Specify a provider-neutral host ceiling and require ACP runtimes/adapters to enforce it before protected tools execute.

options.title: Limit scope to coarse ACPX modes
options.body: Treat this as an enhancement to permission-mode selection only, without claiming path or command containment.

options.title: Defer pending ACP runtime seams
options.body: Wait for the selected ACP runtime hook to stabilize before accepting an OpenClaw configuration contract.

recommendation.title: Define a shared runtime contract
recommendation.body: Specify a provider-neutral host ceiling and require ACP runtimes/adapters to enforce it before protected tools execute.

likelyOwner.reason: Their active adjacent proposal covers the ACPX permission configuration surface that would need to coexist with, but not replace, the restrictive ceiling.
